pos.personaBrief: Spain held 68.2% possession at Euro 2012 and Del Bosque's greatest concern was control (Irish Times); the double pivot and patience against deep teams show possession as defence, though he wanted depth too.

pro.personaBrief: FourFourTwo notes Spain rarely play long balls and counters were slow; he preferred patience against deep teams and safe double-pivot midfielders.

est.personaBrief: His Spain combined in tight spaces with six midfielders and a false nine, with fluid roles around the double pivot, more relational than rigid zones.

lar.personaBrief: The 4-6-0 and the double pivot concentrated play centrally, though full-backs overlapped and wide threats stretched play against Scotland; he looked for gaps patiently.

blo.personaBrief: Spain pressed high with most tackles in the opponent's half (FourFourTwo) and he said they work to win possession back, with good defensive order.

mar.personaBrief: No direct marking evidence; Spain's collective, space-oriented pressing and block suggest zonal principles, with no dedicated man-markers recorded.

pla.personaBrief: He said there is no magic formula, only a plan based on available players, yet Spain kept its control identity against everyone, tweaking such as the no-striker choice vs Italy.

res.personaBrief: He wanted results (house of cards) but also good conduct, humility and playing good football as romantics; Spain controlled games rather than parking the bus.

sis.personaBrief: He adapted tactically to his players and gave roles to stars within a collective plan, tied to the double pivot and balance.

jog.personaBrief: He trusted technical team players in midfield (Busquets, Xabi, Xavi, Iniesta), prioritising control over physical duels.

bas.personaBrief: He kept Casillas and a veteran core to win titles, with continuity and trust in proven players rather than academy-first building.

lid.personaBrief: The man-manager: good relationships are vital, human relations above the sport, one sending-off in 114 matches, though he said coach is not a friend.
